newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bankers want new banking law before polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish bankers want new banking law before polls.

text.p: The Polish Bank Association (ZBP) wants the country's banking regulations overhauled and the central bank charter rewritten before parliamentary polls due around September, its director, Krzysztof Pietraszkiewicz, said on Tuesday.
He said a new banking law under discussion by the finance ministry and central bank was needed to strengthen banks before barriers to international competition were removed at the start of 1999.

"The new banking law and the central bank charter need to be installed before parliamentary polls...as there are only some 600 days left before Poland opens its (banking) borders," Pietraszkiewicz told a news conference.
He said that if new banking regulations were not in place before the polls, the process of forming new government could further delay work on the law.

He said the new banking regulations should reduce the amount of paperwork Polish banks were now required to do and better regulate banking secrecy laws to bring the country's laws in line with those in the European Union.
Pietraszkiewicz said ZBP, which proposed several changes to the draft bill, wanted the new law to better regulate non-banking institutions which did some banking activities, such as trading debt.
He said negotiations between the finance ministry and central bank would probably yield a draft law and be presented to the economic council within weeks.
Pietraszkiewicz said the PZB also supported creating a monetary policy board to decide key policies, a job hitherto done only by the central bank.
He said the board would be apolitical if stringent entry procedures for prospective board candidates were installed.
